### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version

### Module(s)

mini.notify

### Description


I've recently started to test mini.notify and I have a couple of questions. I noticed the beta thread, but I reckoned I might be onto a bug so I chose to open a separate issue.

I've configured mini.notify with `lazy.nvim` like this:

```lua
{
  "echasnovski/mini.notify",
  config = function()
    local mininotify = require "mini.notify"
    mininotify.setup {
      content = {
        format = function(notif)
          return notif.msg
        end,
      },

      lsp_progress = {
        duration_last = 3000,
      },

      window = {
        config = function(buf_id)
          local line_widths = vim.tbl_map(
            vim.fn.strdisplaywidth,
            vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, true)
          )
          local width = 15
          for _, l_w in ipairs(line_widths) do
            width = math.max(width, l_w)
          end

          return {
            width = math.min(width + 1, math.floor(0.9 * vim.o.columns)),
            border = { "┏", " ", " ", " ", " ", " ", "┗", "┃" },
            title = "NOTIFICATIONS",
            title_pos = "right",
          }
        end,
        winblend = 0,
      },
    }

    vim.notify = mininotify.make_notify()
  end,
},
```

Now, the issue is that it seems I'm getting a lot of empty lines in the notifications. E.g., if I open a lua file I immediately get this notification:

![image](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/assets/998898/e4196865-e8a3-4190-916f-fffa2a9cc291)

If I start editing, I will get notifications from the diagnostics:

![image](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/assets/998898/35bca77a-deac-4262-861d-cfab73584999)

Again, notice the empty lines.

----

Also, I was wondering if it might be possible to filter the notifications to avoid showing the same notifications twice. I tried to do this with the `sort` config option, but in the end I gave up.

### Neovim version

NVIM v0.10.0-dev-2047+g8df3742378

### Steps to reproduce

See above description. If necessary, I can attempt to make a minimal version.

### Expected behavior

Don't show empty lines.

### Actual behavior

There are empty lines.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for issue!

> Now, the issue is that it seems I'm getting a lot of empty lines in the notifications.

Not quite a bug, but rather a current documented behavior, which don't think will change. The reason for empty lines is that window's height [is computed assuming default `width`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f54410c7f866f51711118fd82274043cf731b63d/doc/mini-notify.txt#L191-L195). If you want to change either dimension, you'd need to adjust both height and width. This is the reason why `buf_id` is there as input.

> Also, I was wondering if it might be possible to filter the notifications to avoid showing the same notifications twice. I tried to do this with the `sort` config option, but in the end I gave up.

'mini.notify' already won't show same notification twice, but it relies on the internal concept of "sameness" meaning an identifier returned by `MiniNotify.add()`. As `vim.notify()` doesn't have a notion of "notification identifier", output of `make_notify()` treats every notification as unique.

Yes, `content.sort` is the way to [both sort and filter](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f54410c7f866f51711118fd82274043cf731b63d/doc/mini-notify.txt#L138-L139). If you want to not show notifications with duplicating messages, here the way to do this:
```lua
local filterout_duplicates = function(notif_arr)
  local res, present_msg = {}, {}
  for _, notif in ipairs(notif_arr) do
    if not present_msg[notif.msg] then
      table.insert(res, notif)
      present_msg[notif.msg] = true
    end
  end
  return MiniNotify.default_sort(res)
end
require('mini.notify').setup({ content = { sort = filterout_duplicates } })
```
Be careful though: this will not show notifications, but they will still be present until removed. This is only an issue if `MiniNotify.add()` is used directly and not through output of `make_notify()`.

> Not quite a bug, but rather a current documented behavior, which don't think will change. The reason for empty lines is that window's height [is computed assuming default `width`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f54410c7f866f51711118fd82274043cf731b63d/doc/mini-notify.txt#L191-L195). If you want to change either dimension, you'd need to adjust both height and width. This is the reason why `buf_id` is there as input.

Ah, thanks! I agree, I should have read the docs more carefully.

> > Also, I was wondering if it might be possible to filter the notifications to avoid showing the same notifications twice. I tried to do this with the `sort` config option, but in the end I gave up.
> 
> 'mini.notify' already won't show same notification twice, but it relies on the internal concept of "sameness" meaning an identifier returned by `MiniNotify.add()`. As `vim.notify()` doesn't have a notion of "notification identifier", output of `make_notify()` treats every notification as unique.

Ok, I see. I believe the duplicated entries come from the LSP here, though, so not from the regular `vim.notify`?

> Yes, `content.sort` is the way to [both sort and filter](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f54410c7f866f51711118fd82274043cf731b63d/doc/mini-notify.txt#L138-L139). If you want to not show notifications with duplicating messages, here the way to do this: …

Thanks! That was close to what I had, but not quite. I guess my Lua skill needs more work :)

I'll test and see if I like it. I realize that, if I do this, then having the time stamps present makes sense to avoid confusion if some message seems to persist longer than expected.

One more question: Is it possible to format the output with different highlight groups in the formatter? I.e., could I use a different highlight group for the time stamp? (From the docs, I believe the answer is no; if so, would it be hard/possible to add this feature?)

> Ok, I see. I believe the duplicated entries come from the LSP here, though, so not from the regular `vim.notify`?

If you are talking about several "Diagnosing ..." from `lua_ls` then those are from different progress reports which happen to have same message. I checked. Didn't manage to locate the actual issue, though. The overview is that:
- I experience this on large-ish files (1000+ lines) and usually when typing inside comment or string.
- `lua_ls` has hard coded 500ms delay after starting diagnosing buffer to start sending a progress report about it.
- It is usually triggered when Neovim makes request to update semantic tokens.

> One more question: Is it possible to format the output with different highlight groups in the formatter? I.e., could I use a different highlight group for the time stamp? (From the docs, I believe the answer is no; if so, would it be hard/possible to add this feature?)

No, that is not possible and it is deliberate choice to simplify data structures of what `format()` should/might/can return.

*In theory*, having buffer id users can set their own highlighting based on the text:
- The notify buffer has 'mininotify' filetype, so users can create a autocommand for `FileType` event.
- Inside that autocommand another buffer-local autocommand for `TextChanged` can be done to update the highlighting whenever text is changed in that buffer.

Oh, yes; with the `FileType` it would be trivial to just specify a simple `syntax/mininotify.vim` script. I'll consider doing it. Right now, I'm quite happy.

I like your take on this; it seems quite minimal and is still very much "just what I need". Well done!

@lervag, after reconsidering, there is now a [`config.window.max_width_share` option](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/79b1b3350f1cac7cef9e46a637f9adf2a14b4923/doc/mini-notify.txt#L122-L123) to increase maximum allowed width before notification become wrapped. Judging by initial post, you'd benefit from setting it to 0.9.
Cool, thanks! I'm currently specifying both the width and height and have things working very much to my liking, so I don't think I'll be using this now, though.
